title: Specificity
body: Which selector has the highest specificity?
explanation: Specificity is compared as (IDs, classes/attributes/pseudo-classes, elements). `.card .title` is (0,2,0), `ul li a` is (0,0,3). Inline styles and !important override normal rules; `:where()` has zero specificity.

title: box-sizing: border-box

options.t: Content, padding and border (but not margin)

explanation: The default `content-box` adds padding and border on top of width, which makes layouts harder to reason about; many resets apply border-box globally.

title: Flexbox vs Grid
body: When is CSS Grid generally a better fit than Flexbox?

options.t: For one-dimensional alignment of items in a row
For two-dimensional layouts that control rows and columns together
Grid does not support responsive design

answer: Grid is two-dimensional; Flexbox is one-dimensional.
explanation: They complement each other: Grid for page/section layout, Flexbox for distributing items within a component (toolbars, button groups).

title: Centering with Flexbox
body: Which declarations on the parent centre a child horizontally and vertically?

options.t: display: flex; justify-content: center; align-items: center

answer: Flex container with justify-content and align-items set to center.
explanation: With Grid: `display: grid; place-items: center;`. The parent needs a height for vertical centring to be visible.

title: Absolute positioning
body: An element with `position: absolute` is positioned relative to…

options.t: Its nearest positioned ancestor (position other than static), or the initial containing block if none

explanation: Absolutely positioned elements leave normal flow. `position: fixed` is relative to the viewport (unless an ancestor has a transform); `sticky` toggles between relative and fixed.

title: Mobile-first media queries
body: Which media query pattern represents a mobile-first approach?

options.t: Base styles for desktop with max-width overrides
Base styles for small screens, then @media (min-width: …) overrides for larger screens

answer: Min-width breakpoints layered on mobile base styles.
explanation: Mobile-first ships less CSS to small devices and progressively enhances. Container queries let components adapt to their container instead of the viewport.

title: rem vs em
explanation: rem gives predictable sizing that respects user font preferences; em compounds through nested elements.

title: z-index and stacking contexts
body: A modal with `z-index: 9999` still appears below a header with `z-index: 10`. What is the most likely cause?

options.t: The modal is inside an ancestor that creates its own stacking context (e.g. transform, opacity < 1, or positioned with z-index) that is below the header
z-index only works with display: flex

answer: z-index only competes within the same stacking context.
explanation: Properties such as `transform`, `filter`, `opacity < 1`, `position: fixed`, `isolation: isolate` and positioned elements with z-index create stacking contexts. Render modals in a portal at the document root.

title: Margin collapsing
body: Two stacked block elements have `margin-bottom: 20px` and `margin-top: 30px`. What is the vertical gap between them?
answer: 30px — adjacent vertical margins collapse to the larger one.
explanation: Collapsing does not happen in flex or grid containers, with padding or borders in between, or for horizontal margins. Using `gap` in flex/grid layouts avoids the surprise.
